## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two Important defects need fixing: `slugify` drops accented and non-Latin letters, so it fails on realistic page titles, and the PR description leaves out the `## Testing` section that project policy requires.

## Changes
The PR adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify(title)` helper. It lowercases the title, collapses each run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` into one hyphen, and trims hyphens from both ends. The PR also adds a parametrized test in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Keep non-ASCII letters or transliterate them before slugging — `slugify("Café Menu")` returns `"caf-menu"`, and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator. The PR body says it replaces "non-alphanumeric characters", but `é` and `日` are alphanumeric. — Pages with accented titles get wrong URLs, and pages with fully non-Latin titles get an empty slug, so their URLs can collide. — Fix: Either transliterate with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop the combining marks before the regex, or match `[\W_]+` so Unicode letters are kept; then add both titles to the cases in `test_slugify`.
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the PR description — The PR description has no `## Testing` section. AGENTS.md:4 requires: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Without that section, maintainers can't tell from the PR how the change was verified, which the project rule asks every PR to record.
